producer_report.summary: The drain now ends cleanly when a landing leaves `athena.toml` unreadable by the running build. Before, the next item's read failed on the landed file and was counted as that item's failure, so the run stopped as 'repeated failure'. I reproduced it first with the real-steps test, with the new check disabled. Now `Steps::config_after_landing` (default None; `RealSteps` re-reads the config at the new head) is asked right after `Landing::Landed`, still under the landing lock. If the read fails, the job stays landed, `Stop::NeedsReinstall` ('reinstall needed') is set before any other item starts, and rating is skipped because it needs the same config. The report gets a note with the parse error. It says to reinstall Athena (`./setup.sh`) and run `athena drain` again. If the same landing also rebuilt Athena, the stop is `Rebuilt` instead. The root-cause fix is the classification in the drain, not a special case for one key. The new stop is in `Stop::ALL` and in the `drain --help` stop list. CHANGELOG has an entry under Unreleased/Fixed. Tests added: a stub test, a real-steps test with a lander that commits an unknown section and checks the job record is Closed(Landed), a rebuild-wins test, and a genuine-failure regression.

open_issues: Any read error of athena.toml at the new head after a successful landing is treated as 'newer build needed', since a newer schema cannot be told cheaply from other damage. A code comment states this, and the report note includes the parse error text.

I did not test the concurrent drain path (`drain_concurrent`) with max_concurrency above 1. The stop is set under the landing lock, so no new item should start, but an item already past `run_job`'s stop check finishes under the old rules.
I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli`, not the full-workspace `cargo test`; that is left to Athena's checks.
mistakes: My first version of the real-steps test used `Config::parse` and `Records::load_unchecked` in the test, neither of which exists with that shape. I switched to `JobConfig::at` and `Records::load`, and the tests passed afterwards.
I briefly pushed a 'config' entry into the Stub log, which would have broken existing log assertions. I removed it before running any test.
learnings: The false 'repeated failure' comes from the item after the landing, not from the landed job. Its read fails on `JobConfig::at(head)` and the job line says 'not read ... athena.toml does not parse'. The landed job's own record stays Closed(Landed). Nothing in crates/athena-core/src/run/ needs to change.
`display::drain` prints 'stopped <label>: <meaning>' and every note, so a new Stop needs no display.rs change.
Adding a log entry to the test Stub changes the exact-log assertions of many existing tests, so the new Stub method pushes nothing to the log.
The `Lander` trait must be Sync, so a test lander cannot hold the Fixture. It writes and commits through the `athena` argument instead (`athena.git.dir()`).
